title: Apply Theorem 19: Angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circle
show: circle with centre O, points A,B,C on the circle; angle AOB at the centre and angle ACB at the circle on the same arc AB

example.question: $A$, $B$ and $C$ are points on a circle with centre $O$. The angle at the centre is $|\angle AOB| = (6x - 10)^\circ$ and the angle at the circle is $|\angle ACB| = (2x + 5)^\circ$. Both stand on the arc $AB$. Find $x$ and $|\angle ACB|$.

steps.say: Both angles stand on the same arc $AB$. $\hl{1}{|\angle AOB|}$ is at the centre. $\hl{2}{|\angle ACB|}$ is at the circle.
By Theorem 19, the angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circle. So $\hl{1}{|\angle AOB|} = 2\hl{2}{|\angle ACB|}$.
Multiply out the bracket, then collect the $x$ terms on one side.
Substitute $x = 10$ into the angle at the circle.

title: Construction 4: Line perpendicular to a line l through a point on l
show: compass-and-straight-edge construction: line l with point P on it, arcs and the perpendicular through P, with arcs left visible

example.question: Draw a line $l$ and mark a point $P$ on it. Construct the line through $P$ perpendicular to $l$.

steps.say: Put the compass point on $P$. Draw an arc that cuts $l$ on each side of $P$. Call the points $A$ and $B$.

rows.aside: Keep the compass setting the same for both arcs, so $|PA| = |PB|$.

steps.say: Open the compass wider than $|PA|$. With the point on $A$, draw an arc above the line.

rows.aside: Do not change the setting yet.

steps.say: Keep the same setting. With the point on $B$, draw an arc that crosses the first one. Call the crossing $Q$.

rows.aside: Leave all arcs on the page. They are the construction lines.

steps.say: With the ruler, draw a straight line from $P$ through $Q$.

title: Solve a linear inequality
show: number line with a closed dot at -2 and everything to the left shaded (x≤-2)

steps.say: Multiply every term in the bracket by $-3$. Watch the signs.
Subtract $7$ from both sides. Do the same thing to both sides and the sign does not change.
Divide both sides by $-3$. That is a **negative**, so the sign flips from $\ge$ to $\le$.

title: Solve a combined (double) linear inequality
show: number line with closed dot at -4 and open dot at 3 and the segment between shaded

steps.say: The $x$ is stuck with a $+3$. Subtract $3$ from all three parts, so the inequality stays balanced.
Now divide all three parts by $2$. It is positive, so the signs stay the same way round.

rows.aside: Dividing by a negative number would flip the signs. Here it does not.

steps.say: $x$ is at least $\hl{1}{-4}$ and less than $\hl{2}{3}$. A $\le$ includes the end point, a $<$ leaves it out.

title: Solve a quadratic inequality
show: upward parabola y=2x²-5x-12 crossing the x-axis at x=-1.5 and 4, with the part on or below the axis shaded and the interval -1.5≤x≤4 marked on a number line

steps.say: Treat it as an equation first. Factorise $2x^2 - 5x - 12$ to find where it equals zero.
The roots are where each bracket is zero. They are the end points of the interval.
The $x^2$ term is positive, so the graph is a U. It dips below the axis between the roots. We want $\le 0$, so we want the part between $\hl{1}{-\tfrac{3}{2}}$ and $\hl{2}{4}$.

rows.aside: Check $x = 0$: $-12 \le 0$, true. It lies inside the interval.

title: Solve modulus inequalities
show: number line showing x≤-1 and x≥4 shaded with closed dots

steps.say: A modulus that is at least $5$ means the inside is at least $5$ **or** at most $-5$. Write both.
Add $3$ to both sides, then divide by $2$.
Do the same with the other inequality. The sign stays the same way round, because $2$ is positive.
Both pieces are answers. Join them with **or**, never with and.

rows.aside: Check $x = 5$: $|7| = 7 \ge 5$. It works. Check $x = 0$: $|-3| = 3$, not $\ge 5$. It is left out.
